### Motivation
- Convert existing standalone “Subscribe” CTAs into working email signup forms using Formspree AJAX so users remain on-page and receive inline success/error feedback on this static GitHub Pages site.

### Description
- Replaced standalone Subscribe buttons with inline forms (email input on the left + submit button on the right) and gave each form a unique ID (`subscribe-form-*`) across the site; files updated: `index.html`, `stashbox_hub/index.html`, `artist_spotlight/index.html`, `the_feed/index.html`, `shop/index.html`, and `official_merch/index.html`.
- Added inline success and error containers (`data-fs-success`, `data-fs-error`) and a hidden `source_page` field for attribution on every new form instance.
- Injected a small, page-local `.subscribe-wrapper` CSS block in each modified file to preserve existing styles and ensure responsive layout with the input to the left of the CTA.
- Bootstrapped the Formspree AJAX CDN once per page and initialized each form separately with `formspree('initForm', { formElement: '#subscribe-form-UNIQUE', formId: 'xgopdgea' });` (no redirect-based POSTs are used).

### Testing
- Searched the codebase with `rg` to find any remaining standalone `Subscribe` buttons and confirmed there are no remaining standalone Subscribe buttons outside the new form pattern (success).
- Verified each modified file includes the Formspree CDN script and the corresponding `formspree('initForm', ...)` calls via `rg` (success).
- Attempted a structural validation using Python + `BeautifulSoup` but the environment lacked `bs4`, so that automated parse step failed and was skipped (warning).
- Manual tally from the updates: converted and wired a total of `12` subscribe/signup form instances across the site (verified by grepping for `subscribe-form-`).

body:
The existing `scripts/` directory only contains bash scripts, making them unusable on Windows without WSL. This adds a `.ps1` counterpart for each `.sh` script with identical behaviour.

## New scripts

| PowerShell | Mirrors |
|---|---|
| `exp_a_baseline.ps1` | `exp_a_baseline.sh` |
| `exp_b_cycada.ps1` | `exp_b_cycada.sh` |
| `exp_b_cyclegan.ps1` | `exp_b_cyclegan.sh` |
| `exp_c_awada.ps1` | `exp_c_awada.sh` |
| `exp_d_oracle.ps1` | `exp_d_oracle.sh` |

## Key bash → PowerShell translations

| Bash | PowerShell |
|---|---|
| `set -euo pipefail` | `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` + exit-code guard after each `python` call |
| `BENCHMARK=${1:-sim10k_to_cityscapes}` | `param([string]$Benchmark = "sim10k_to_cityscapes")` |
| `mkdir -p "$DIR"` | `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Dir \| Out-Null` |
| `ls -t "$DIR"/*.pth \| head -1` | `Get-ChildItem \| Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending \| Select-Object -First 1` |
| Conditional inline arg `$([ ... ] && echo "--classes car")` | Array-based arg list built with an `if` block |

## Usage

```powershell
# Run from the repo root — same arguments as the bash counterparts
.\scripts\exp_a_baseline.ps1 sim10k_to_cityscapes
.\scripts\exp_c_awada.ps1 cityscapes_to_foggy
```

body:
## Summary
- Introduces complete versioning and release system for Tandemu OSS (starting at v0.1.0)
- Backend version endpoints: `GET /api/health/version`, `GET /api/health/version/check` (checks GitHub Releases), `POST /api/health/update` (triggers Watchtower)
- Frontend: UpdateBanner component with one-click update + System card on Settings page
- Docker Compose: switches to GHCR published images + Watchtower sidecar for container auto-updates
- GitHub Actions: CI workflow (lint/build/docker) + Release workflow (tag push → Docker build → GHCR → GitHub Release)
- Release automation via `release-it` with conventional-changelog and bumper plugins
- SaaS gating: all update UI hidden when `BILLING_ENABLED=true`

## Update flow
1. `pnpm release-it` → bumps version, generates CHANGELOG, tags, creates GitHub Release
2. Tag push triggers GitHub Actions → builds + pushes Docker images to GHCR
3. Self-hosted admin sees "v0.2.0 available" on Settings page
4. Clicks "Update Now" → backend triggers Watchtower → pulls new images + restarts
5. Migrations auto-run on startup, frontend reloads

## Test plan
- [ ] `GET /api/health/version` returns `{ "version": "0.1.0" }`
- [ ] `GET /api/health/version/check` fetches GitHub Releases and compares
- [ ] Settings page shows System card with current version (only on OSS, not SaaS)
- [ ] UpdateBanner appears when a newer GitHub Release exists
- [ ] `POST /api/health/update` triggers Watchtower or returns manual instructions
- [ ] `pnpm release-it --dry-run` shows version bump preview
- [ ] GitHub Actions workflows have valid syntax
- [ ] `docker-compose.yml` references GHCR images correctly

Closes SGS-176

author: p1r473
body:
The current firewall import whitelist and firewall import blacklist logic only accepts lines that are only a CIDR.

Any line with a trailing inline comment or no CIDR range is silently discarded.

Example entries that fail silently today:
```
170.114.0.0/16 #Zoom
137.221.104.0/22 #Battle.net / Blizzard
166.117.0.0/16 #Battle.net
166.117.0.0
```

This leads to:
**Import reporting success
Entries appearing partially imported
Some expected CIDRs missing from the active ipset
Traffic still being blocked unexpectedly**

**Root Cause**
Import logic uses a strict anchored regex:

^...$

This requires the entire line to match an IP/CIDR and does not tolerate trailing content such as comments.

**Solution**
Strip inline comments and blank lines before validation.

This:
- Removes trailing # comments
- Removes empty lines
- Preserves existing IP/CIDR validation logic

**Behavior After Change**
These entries now import correctly:
```
170.114.0.0/16 #Zoom
137.221.104.0/22 #Battle.net / Blizzard
166.117.0.0/16 #Battle.net / Hybrid Networks
166.117.0.0
```
Entries appear in whitelist view imported
Entries populate the active ipset
Matching traffic is no longer blocked

Notes: the whitelist I am importing is my own here https://github.com/p1r473/ipblocklist/blob/main/ipwhitelist.txt

author: sokra
body:
### What?

Optimizes the `get_compilation_issues` MCP tool to use a single whole-app module graph computation instead of iterating all endpoint groups and computing per-route module graphs individually.

### Why?

The `get_compilation_issues` MCP tool was too slow for large apps because `get_all_compilation_issues_inner_operation` called `endpoint_group.module_graphs()` for every endpoint group, computing separate per-route module graphs. This is O(routes) graph computations when a single whole-app graph would suffice.

The reason the original code didn't use `whole_app_module_graphs()` was that it calls `drop_issues()` in development mode (to prevent every route from re-reporting all issues during HMR). This would suppress the issues the MCP tool needs to collect.

### How?

- **New method `Project::whole_app_module_graphs_without_dropping_issues()`** — calls the same underlying `whole_app_module_graph_operation` (the `#[turbo_tasks::function(operation, root)]` computation) but connects the result without dropping issues. Issues propagate normally so callers can collect them.
- **`get_all_compilation_issues_inner_operation`** now calls this new method instead of iterating endpoint groups, reducing the work to a single graph computation.
- **Extracted `scale_down_node_pool` helper** — the Node.js process pool scale-down logic (shared between both `whole_app_module_graphs` variants) is extracted into a free function to avoid duplication.
- **Existing `whole_app_module_graphs()`** is unchanged in behavior — still drops issues in dev mode for HMR per-route subscriptions.

author: djdanielsson
body:
## Summary
- Propose ADR-051: two new optional validator services for inline dependency health assessment during scans
- Collection Health Validator scans installed collections with a curated rule subset (galaxy metadata, module/role quality, FQCN usage, deprecated patterns)
- Python Dependency Auditor runs pip-audit against session venvs to surface known CVEs

## Changes
- Add `.sdlc/adrs/ADR-051-dependency-health-scanning.md` — full ADR with context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and implementation notes
- Update `.sdlc/adrs/README.md` — add ADR-051 to Proposed section, bump next-available number

## Key design points
- Both validators follow the Gitleaks optional-validator pattern: env-gated gRPC address, `Validator.Validate` + `Validator.Health` contract, `run_in_executor()` for blocking work, graceful degradation when unavailable
- Collection health findings reuse existing rule IDs (L0xx, M0xx, R1xx) with `RuleScope.COLLECTION` differentiation; Python CVE findings use new `R200` rule ID
- Persistent cache for collection scans keyed on `(fqcn, version, cache_schema)` — auto-invalidates when rules change
- Complements REQ-010 enterprise sidecar without replacing it — inline findings during scan vs. fleet-wide aggregation
- No proto changes needed; no architectural invariants modified

## Copilot review fixes
- **c16ded0**: Removed non-existent R102 rule; reconciled offline pip-audit guidance; fixed `_OPTIONAL_SERVICES` dict structure
- **9dd1773**: Added missing supplier field to venv introspection descriptions; replaced L012/L013 with actual role rules L027/L053/L077/L079
- **f194652**: Added `cache_schema` to collection health cache key for rule-change invalidation; disambiguated `pip-audit -l/--local` from offline database mode

## Test plan
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (adr-index validated)
- [x] ADR follows project template and conventions
- [x] ADR index updated with correct entry and next-available number
- [x] No conflicts with existing ADRs (consistent with ADR-008, ADR-009, ADR-010, ADR-040, REQ-010)
- [x] All Copilot review comments addressed and resolved (8/8)

body:
This PR updates [Django](https://pypi.org/project/Django) from **2.1.5** to **6.0.4**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.4
   ```
   ==========================

*April 7, 2026*

Django 6.0.4 fixes one security issue with severity "moderate", four security
issues with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-3902: ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation
====================================================================

``ASGIRequest`` normalizes header names following WSGI conventions, mapping
hyphens to underscores. As a result, even in configurations where reverse
proxies carefully strip security-sensitive headers named with hyphens, such a
header could be spoofed by supplying a header named with underscores.

Under WSGI, it is the responsibility of the server or proxy to avoid ambiguous
mappings. (Django's :djadmin:`runserver` was patched in :cve:`2015-0219`.) But
under ASGI, there is not the same uniform expectation, even if many proxies
protect against this under default configuration (including ``nginx`` via
``underscores_in_headers off;``).

Headers containing underscores are now ignored by ``ASGIRequest``, matching the
behavior of :pypi:`Daphne <daphne>`, the reference server for ASGI.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4277: Privilege abuse in ``GenericInlineModelAdmin``
=============================================================

Add permissions on inline model instances were not validated on submission of
forged ``POST`` data in
:class:`~django.contrib.contenttypes.admin.GenericInlineModelAdmin`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4292: Privilege abuse in ``ModelAdmin.list_editable``
==============================================================

Admin changelist forms using
:attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_editable` incorrectly allowed new
instances to be created via forged ``POST`` data.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33033: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``MultiPartParser`` via base64-encoded file upload
===============================================================================================================

When using ``django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser``, multipart uploads
with ``Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`` that include excessive whitespace
may trigger repeated memory copying, potentially degrading performance.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33034: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass
=========================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit when reading
``HttpRequest.body``, potentially loading an unbounded request body into
memory and causing service degradation.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 where :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogin`
  and :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogout` did not respectively set or clear
  ``request.user`` if it had already been materialized (e.g., by sync
  middleware) (:ticket:`37017`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 in admin forms where
  ``RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`` incorrectly wrapped all widgets in a
  ``<fieldset>`` (:ticket:`36949`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where the ``fields.E348`` system check did not
  detect name clashes between model managers and
  :attr:`~django.db.models.ForeignKey.related_name`\s for non-self-referential
  relationships (:ticket:`36973`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.3
   ```
   ==========================

*March 3, 2026*

Django 6.0.3 fixes a security issue with severity "moderate", a security issue
with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.2.

CVE-2026-25673: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``URLField`` via Unicode normalization on Windows
==============================================================================================================

The :class:`~django.forms.URLField` form field's ``to_python()`` method used
:func:`~urllib.parse.urlsplit` to determine whether to prepend a URL scheme to
the submitted value. On Windows, ``urlsplit()`` performs
:func:`NFKC normalization <python:unicodedata.normalize>`, which can be
disproportionately slow for large inputs containing certain characters.

``URLField.to_python()`` now uses a simplified scheme detection, avoiding
Unicode normalization entirely and deferring URL validation to the appropriate
layers. As a result, while leading and trailing whitespace is still stripped by
default, characters such as newlines, tabs, and other control characters within
the value are no longer handled by ``URLField.to_python()``. When using the
default :class:`~django.core.validators.URLValidator`, these values will
continue to raise :exc:`~django.core.exceptions.ValidationError` during
validation, but if you rely on custom validators, ensure they do not depend on
the previous behavior of ``URLField.to_python()``.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-25674: Potential incorrect permissions on newly created file system objects
====================================================================================

Django's file-system storage and file-based cache backends used the process
``umask`` to control permissions when creating directories. In multi-threaded
environments, one thread's temporary umask change can affect other threads'
file and directory creation, resulting in file system objects being created
with unintended permissions.

Django now applies the requested permissions via :func:`~os.chmod` after
:func:`~os.mkdir`, removing the dependency on the process-wide umask.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed :exc:`NameError` when inspecting functions making use of deferred
  annotations in Python 3.14 (:ticket:`36903`).

* Fixed :exc:`AttributeError` when subclassing builtin lookups and neglecting
  to :ref:`override<tuple-for-params>` ``as_sql()`` to accept any sequence
  (:ticket:`36934`).

* Fixed :exc:`TypeError` when deprecation warnings are emitted in environments
  importing Django by namespace (:ticket:`36961`).

* Fixed a visual regression where fieldset legends were misaligned in the admin
  (:ticket:`36920`).

* Prevented the :data:`django.tasks.signals.task_finished` signal from writing
  extraneous log messages when no exceptions are encountered (:ticket:`36951`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.2
   ```
   ==========================

*February 3, 2026*

Django 6.0.2 fixes three security issues with severity "high", two security
issues with severity "moderate", one security issue with severity "low", and
several bugs in 6.0.1.

CVE-2025-13473: Username enumeration through timing difference in mod_wsgi authentication handler
=================================================================================================

The ``django.contrib.auth.handlers.modwsgi.check_password()`` function for
:doc:`authentication via mod_wsgi</howto/deployment/wsgi/apache-auth>`
allowed remote attackers to enumerate users via a timing attack.

This issue has severity "low"

author: ehotting
body:
> **Status (2026-07-12): draft, superseded. Do not merge.**
>
> The guards described below stop the assert, but they silently omit one layer's K and V from the saved state. Measured on current master: exactly 151,576 bytes missing, which is one layer's K plus V. The root cause is an uninitialised view after a Vulkan buffer split (`suballocation_block_size`, default 1 GiB), and it should be fixed in the allocator.
>
> Full reproduction, instrumentation and measurements: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/21576#issuecomment-4950623433
>
> Kept open as a tracker until a root fix lands (@Yoshi4470's `99655d5` or an equivalent). See also #23737 and #19839.

---

K and V tensors in `layer.k_stream`/`v_stream` can have `tensor->data == NULL` if the tensor object exists but has no GPU memory allocated. The existing V loops guarded for `!v` but not `!v->data`, and the K loops had no guard at all, causing `GGML_ASSERT(tensor->data != NULL)` in `ggml_backend_tensor_get` during cache state save/restore.

Add `!tensor->data` null guards matching the existing pattern for both K and V tensors in `state_write_data` and `state_read_data`.

## Overview

Related to #21468

I ran into this running Gemma 4 26B-A4B with cache reuse and multiple slots. The server would crash with SIGABRT every few minutes. Both write and read paths in `llama_kv_cache` iterate all layers but some K/V tensors have `data == NULL`. The write path for V already had `if (!v) continue` but K had no guard. Both lacked a check for `tensor->data`.

## Additional information

Tested on Gemma 4 26B-A4B, Vulkan backend, 4 slots, cache reuse enabled. 20/20 multi-turn requests stable, previously crashed every 4-5 min.

No impact on models without iSWA since all tensors are fully allocated and the guards never trigger.

## Requirements

- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES - AI assisted in finding the root cause and setting up local testing.

### Motivation
- Decouple model-representation and export logic from `MainWindow` by encapsulating it into dedicated services so the MainWindow surface remains a thin wrapper. 
- Reduce direct coupling to generated `Ui::MainWindow` by having services accept explicit widget and `Simulator` dependencies.

### Description
- Added service constructors and stateful members so `ModelLanguageSynchronizer`, `GraphvizModelExporter`, and `CppModelExporter` now accept `Simulator` and the specific Qt widgets they operate on (e.g. `QPlainTextEdit`, `QLabel`, `QCheckBox`) and store them as members. 
- Updated `MainWindow` to construct these services with the required dependencies and to pass a callback for post-model-creation event wiring via `ModelLanguageSynchronizer`'s constructor. 
- Removed direct `Ui::MainWindow` usage from service implementations and converted previous static/wrapper calls in `mainwindow.cpp`/`mainwindow_modelrepresentations.cpp` to call the new service methods (e.g. `actualizeModelSimLanguage()`, `createModelImage()`, `actualizeModelCppCode()`, `setSimulationModelBasedOnText()`). 
- Cleaned up headers and includes (forward-declared Qt widget types where appropriate) and preserved legacy behaviors (DOT name adjustments, code indentation, file-based DOT -> PNG flow, message-box error reporting) while relocating logic into the service classes.

body:
Все, внутри станции или снаружи, постоянно используют hardsuit. Броня, которую вы получаете при спавне, кажется бесполезной. Я ни разу не видел, чтобы кто-то носил обычную броню внутри станции. Поэтому я представляю вам это обновление.

Классические бронежилеты фракций, страдающих от рейдов на станцию (НЕ HARDSUIT, А ОБЫЧНАЯ БРОНЯ), были слегка усилены. Это обновление касается только ЛРНП и БМС — броня этих двух фракций усилена в тестовом режиме. К защите от пробития (piercing protection) добавлено всего +10 к защите от урона.

Учитывая, что эту броню нельзя использовать в космосе, это отличное обновление для боёв внутри станции. Также броня этих двух фракций теперь сделана из керамики, поэтому она быстрее изнашивается и требует ремонта.

Теперь во время рейдов на станцию вы сможете защищать себя с помощью этой брони.

Также Knight Templar suit’ы были возвращены к своей прежней силе. Ранее они были чрезмерно ослаблены из-за наличия ночного видения. Теперь они снова возвращаются с усиленной защитой от пробития. Однако их скорость снижена, а защита от heat и caustic урона уменьшена.

Это уже не те универсальные костюмы — комбинации скорость + броня + ночное зрение больше нет, теперь у них есть только дополнительная броня. Тем не менее, они всё ещё сильнее обычной брони БМС.

Эти костюмы нельзя производить — в БМС их всего 3, и они дают уникальный опыт для фракции. Поэтому я считаю это справедливым. Сейчас в МС почти никто не берёт эти роли, и я думаю, что это изменение сделает их более привлекательными.

### Motivation

- Provide a complete starter LMS app implementing course/lesson pages, a dashboard, and a cyberpunk-themed UI.
- Add backend features for user authentication, progress tracking and server-side quiz evaluation to support interactive learning flows.
- Introduce Prisma schema and seed data to enable an out-of-the-box local database for development and Vercel-friendly deployment. 

### Description

author: sroecker
body:
## Problem

Commit `cc2b56b2` changed the `tool_progress_callback` signature from:
```python
callback(name, preview, args)  # 3 args
```
to:
```python  
callback(event_type, name, preview, args, **kwargs)  # 4+ args
```

However, the API server's chat completion streaming callback (`_on_tool_progress`) was **not updated**, causing tool calls to not display in Open WebUI.

### What went wrong
When the agent called:
```python
tool_progress_callback("tool.started", "web_search", "query: foo", {...})
```

The API server interpreted:
- `name` = `"tool.started"` (the event type!)
- `preview` = `"web_search"` (the actual tool name)
- `args` = `"query: foo"` (the preview text)

This broke the `name.startswith("_")` check and displayed the wrong information.

## Fix

Updated `_on_tool_progress` in `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` to:
1. Accept the new 4-argument signature `(event_type, name, preview, args, **kwargs)`
2. Filter for `event_type == "tool.started"` to only show tool start events
3. Accept `**kwargs` for optional `duration`/`is_error` parameters

## Testing

- [x] Tool calls now display correctly in Open WebUI
- [x] Verified the fix matches the pattern used in `_make_run_event_callback` (line 1328)

---
**Note:** This fix is minimal and only affects the Open WebUI streaming path. The `/v1/runs` endpoint already had the correct signature from the original commit.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide end-to-end support for routine reordering so users can change order in the Manage Routines page and have that order persist locally and sync to the backend. 
- Ensure the Today page and storage layer respect the user-defined `sortOrder` while keeping `localStorage` authoritative (optimistic local updates with background sync). 
- Add focused unit coverage for the reorder logic in the storage layer.

### Description
- Added `routinesApi.reorder(orderedIds: string[])` in `client/src/lib/storage.ts` that performs an optimistic local reorder, assigns sequential `sortOrder` values, persists to `localStorage`, and fire-and-forget syncs to `PUT /api/routines/reorder`.
- Updated `routinesApi.getAll()` to sort by `sortOrder` first, then by active state when ties occur.
- Implemented a new worker endpoint `PUT /api/routines/reorder` in `worker/src/index.ts` (registered before `PUT /api/routines/:id`) that validates `orderedIds`, requires `X-User-Id`, and batch-updates `sort_order` for the authenticated user's routines in D1.
- Updated the Routines page (`client/src/pages/routines.tsx`) to add a left-edge `GripVertical` handle, native drag/drop interactions (handle-initiated), keyboard up/down reorder support from the handle, visual drag/drop states, and a reorder mutation with a success toast; handles are shown only when there are 2+ routines.
- Updated Today page grouping (`client/src/pages/today.tsx`) to sort routines within each time-category by `sortOrder`.
- Added unit tests `client/src/lib/storage.test.ts` that verify sequential `sortOrder` assignment after reorder, single-item no-op behavior, metadata preservation, and that the correct API payload is sent for bulk reorder.
- Note: attempting to install the originally-proposed `@dnd-kit/*` packages failed in this environment (registry 403), so a no-new-dependency native drag/drop + keyboard fallback was implemented while preserving the intended storage and API contract.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests with `npm run test` and they passed (`vitest` run: 2 test files, 23 tests total passed).
- Ran static type checks with `npm run check` (`tsc`) and it succeeded.
- The added storage unit tests (`client/src/lib/storage.test.ts`) were executed as part of the test run and passed.

author: svalat
body:
To the indi team : Feel free to edit and comment the patch, this is a proposal.

The problem
-------------------

As discussed in #1239 I had some issues with the celetronaux driver with my **Celestron CG5** + **Celestron SkyPortal Dongle WiFi** to enable autoguiding.

The **celestronaux** driver currently send the `PULSE` command to the mount which are not taken in account by my setup.

At the opposite, running with **Celestron CPWI** + **PH2** shows that the `PULSE` command are replaced by commands updating the `guide rate` (`MC_SET_POS_GUIDERATE` and `MC_SET_NEG_GUIDERATE`) by shifting it about a percentage of the sideral speed (80% by default).

All the analysis of the problem can be fount in #1239 by tracking the packets send to the mount by **CPWI**.

By the way, the **EQMod** driver also implement this approach.

This patch
---------------

I implemented the solution in the CelestronAux driver as an optional feature which needs to be enabled in the contrôle panel of the mount named **PULSE_MODE** and which offer two values :

-`PUSLE` : the default, corresponding the current implementation, still valid and in place.
-`GUIDE RATE` to be enabled on demand to enable the **guide rate drife** approach of **EQMod** and **CPWI**.

impact to the user
---------------------------

No impact by default, if the mount do not react to `PULSE` mode the user has to enable the `GUIDE RATE` mode.

The selected mode is saved as other values to enabled again on restart.

The implementation
------------------------------

I added a few states to the driver to track the status of the guiding and to restore (`restoreTrackingRateMode()`) it to its normal value when the pulse has been done.

The delay is tracked by two new timers, one for each axis. Note that if a pulse ingoing and a new one arrive, I extend the duration of the pulse.

I added a check about the hemisphere (` if (isNorthHemisphere() == false)`), to be checked. At this location I'm not sure of the sign of the existing line : 

```cpp
//for east
guidePulse(AXIS_RA, ms, -rate);
//for west
guidePulse(AXIS_RA, ms, rate);
```

But to reproduce **CPWI** behavior I need to invert this sign (I currently let in this patch the old way).
In practice this is not a big issue because PHD2 auto adap to the moves when it trains itself.

To look at
--------------

I arbitary limit the pulse time to 10 seconds (10000 ms) as there was already a limit on PULSE probably due to hardware limitations. In practice this limit is not required but avoids possible issues if for some reason the user set manually an hour which might be not desired because we cannot stop it once it is triggered.

Validation
--------------

I passed 3 full nights with a draft of this patch + 1 full night with this cleaned one.

The validation setup is : 

- Telescope : Celestron C8
- Mount : Celestron CG5
- Contrôle : Via SkyPortal Celestron WiFi dongle
- Tracking cam : Altaïr GPCAM 462M2 with OAG
- Tracking: PHD2 (version 2.6.14)
- OS: Gentoo
- Version: latest (on ARM on Raspberry-PI).
- Indlib : 2.1.7
- Kstars : 3.8.0

author: copilot
body:
`ClearanceOverlayView` rendered clearance zones but gave no spatial signal for *where* a conflict exists — only that one does. This PR makes conflict areas spatially explicit and adds directional context throughout the clearance surface.

## ClearanceEngine

- **`ClearanceStatus.displayMessage`** updated to outcome-first language: `"Pass — …"` / `"Tight fit — …"` / `"Blocked — …"`
- **New `ClearanceStatus.shortLabel`**: `"Pass"` / `"Tight fit"` / `"Blocked"` for compact banners and accessibility
- **`ClearanceIssue.sideLabel: String?`** — new optional field (default `nil`, backward-compat) carrying the affected side: `"front"`, `"left"`, `"right"`, `"top"`, `"bottom"`
- **`wallProximityIssues`** populates `sideLabel` by comparing wall distances; tighter side wins

## ClearanceOverlayView

- **Intrusion regions**: `intrusionRects(of:roomBounds:)` computes sub-rects of `serviceAccessRect` that extend outside normalised room bounds `[0,1]` — these are the wall-blocked areas
- **Diagonal hatch fill**: `drawHatch(into:rect:color:)` clips a context copy and strokes 45° lines — gives a non-colour conflict signal for accessibility
- **Room boundary outline** drawn behind the halos so intrusion areas are visually anchored
- **Stronger footprint**: stroke `2 → 2.5 pt`, fill opacity `0.20 → 0.25`
- **Tappable badge**: icon varies by severity (`xmark.circle` vs `exclamationmark.triangle`); tap opens `ClearanceIssueSheet`
- **`ClearanceIssueSheet`**: lists each issue with direction label, severity icon, confidence note, and appliance guidance
- **Legend** gains a "Wall conflict" hatch-swatch entry when intrusions are present
- `hatchSpacing` / `hatchLineWidth` extracted as named constants

## SessionCaptureView

- Summary row now stacks `shortLabel` (bold) over `displayMessage` (caption), with direction hints (`"front · left"`) replacing the bare issue count when sides are known

## Tests

9 new `ClearanceEngineTests` covering `shortLabel` values, outcome-first `displayMessage` prefixes, `sideLabel` population for all issue kinds, left/right directional accuracy, and `nil` default backward compatibility.

body:
## Summary

Bug 3 from discovery 2026-04-05. `UploadStagingProvider` was mounted once with the `x-project-id` header baked into `useUploadThing`'s config; the header closure did not refresh on cross-project navigation, causing files to land on the original project after the user moved to another project without a full page reload.

## Changes

- **`UploadStagingProvider`** — `key={projectId}` forces remount on project change so the header closure picks up the new ID
- **`useIntakeStaging`** — same pattern via `key={projectId}` on `UnifiedIntakeModal` in `ProjectLayoutClient.tsx`
- **Dev-mode tripwires** in both providers that loud-fail (`console.error`) if `projectId` changes without a remount — catches any future regression that drops the `key` prop

## Reproduction

1. Open project A → DMS tab
2. Navigate (no reload) to project B → DMS tab
3. Drop a file

**Pre-fix:** file lands on project A
**Post-fix:** file lands on project B

## Evidence

`core_doc` row 568 (Peregrine PDF landed on project 161 instead of 162).

## Notes

- Server-side ownership check (`userOwnsProject`) intentionally not touched in this PR — defensive Referer validation and the legacy NULL-owner bypass are addressed in #2 (JWT signature verification).

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual repro per steps above on a Vercel preview deploy
- [ ] Verify the dev-mode tripwire console.errors when forcing a projectId mismatch
- [ ] Confirm `core_doc` rows land on the correct project after cross-project navigation

body:
## Summary
- Duration extraction is moved out of `FileCollector` into the checkers, where each file is already loaded in memory — scanning no longer opens every file twice.
- On HDD the scan is now dramatically faster: a single `FileInfo.Length` call per file instead of one `FileInfo` + one metadata-reader file open.
- `IFormatChecker.Check` now returns `CheckOutcome(CheckResult, TimeSpan?)`; the duration flows through `FileCompletedEventArgs` to the UI.
- The Duration column and total duration status are populated progressively during analysis instead of at scan time — explicit UX tradeoff accepted for the perf win.

## Notes
- FLAC (native + process) derives duration from `STREAMINFO` which was already being read.
- MP3 uses a new `ReadOnlySpan<byte>` overload in `Mp3MetadataReader` that parses the in-memory buffer directly (no re-open, no allocation-heavy copy).
- Version bumped to 1.1.6.

## Test plan
- [ ] Load a large folder from the HDD — scan completes noticeably faster than before
- [ ] Start analysis — Duration column fills in as each file completes
- [ ] Status bar total duration grows during analysis and matches previous behavior at the end
- [ ] Re-running analysis on the same queue resets the total cleanly

body:
**💡 What**: Implemented `requests.Session()` to enable HTTP connection pooling within the `Scraper` class, reusing TCP connections and TLS handshakes across multiple requests.
**🎯 Why**: The web scraper was previously making individual `requests.get` calls for every URL visited, forcing a new connection and handshake each time. This introduces significant network overhead when repeatedly crawling pages on the same domain.
**📊 Impact**: Substantially reduces latency and overall execution time for deep scrapes. Avoids quadratic network latency scaling purely driven by connection setups.
**🔬 Measurement**: To verify the improvement, run a large multi-depth crawl against a domain. Network performance tools or application metrics will reflect significantly faster response times per page after the initial TLS setup. Tests were updated and verified.

author: siltus
body:
## Problem

Deleting items from the database is slow — each deletion issues N individual \DELETE WHERE id=X\ queries per table (media, color, kphash, matrix), plus a disk fsync per commit. Deleting 10 items could mean 40+ individual queries.

## Changes

### 1. Batch DELETE with IN-clause
Instead of looping \DELETE FROM table WHERE id=X\ per item, builds \DELETE FROM table WHERE id IN (1,2,3,...)\ with batches of 500 (SQLite parameter limit safe). Reduces query count from N to \ceil(N/500)\ per table.

### 2. PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL
Set on every connection. Reduces fsync overhead — still crash-safe with WAL journal, but doesn't wait for every commit to physically hit disk.

### 3. Updated all removeRecords() implementations
\ColorDescIndex\, \DctFeaturesIndex\, and \CvFeaturesIndex\ all updated to accept pre-built batch strings. Old \QVector<int>\ signature preserved as convenience overload in the base class.

## Files changed
- \src/database.cpp\ — batch building, synchronous pragma
- \src/index.h\ — new batched overload + convenience wrapper
- \src/colordescindex.cpp/.h\ — batched delete for color table
- \src/dctfeaturesindex.cpp/.h\ — batched delete for kphash table
- \src/cvfeaturesindex.cpp/.h\ — batched delete for matrix table

body:
Add a configurable fallback_to_local option to prevent silent LocalAdapter degradation

When a horizontal adapter (Redis, NATS, Kafka, etc.) fails to initialize, the server silently falls back to LocalAdapter, breaking cross-node features like presence channels. Add adapter.fallback_to_local config option (default: true for backward compatibility) that, when set to false, causes the server to crash on adapter init failure instead of silently degrading.

Env override: ADAPTER_FALLBACK_TO_LOCAL=false

author: jbdel
body:
This PR improves the offline SVS training path by reusing `OpenSlide` objects in `SlideDataset` and by forwarding the configured DataLoader worker settings for non-streaming training.

## Current changes

- `SlideDataset` now uses a module-level LRU cache for `OpenSlide` objects in both `get_all` and `__getitem__`.
- The cache is capped at `_SLIDE_CACHE_LIMIT = 512` per worker process. Evicted slides are closed immediately, and an `atexit` hook closes anything still cached when the worker exits.
- The cache lookup is inlined at the call sites to match the repo preference in `AGENTS.md` against small helper functions.
- The offline SVS DataLoader now passes `persistent_workers=cfg.train.num_workers > 0`.
- The offline SVS DataLoader now passes `prefetch_factor=cfg.train.prefetch_factor`, so this remains YAML-configured and fail-loud instead of using a fallback default.

## Why this is useful

The old `SlideDataset.__getitem__` opened `OpenSlide(path)` for every sampled patch. Python OpenSlide closes objects when they are deleted, so the previous wording about leaking thousands of file descriptors was too strong. The practical issue is repeated OpenSlide object creation and close churn across millions of sampled patches, with no reuse when the sampler returns to a recently used slide.

The new code keeps reuse bounded and explicit: cache hits reuse an existing slide handle, misses open a slide, and LRU eviction closes the oldest cached slide. This should help small 1-GPU runs where data loading is visible, while keeping memory growth controlled for larger multi-GPU H100 runs with many DataLoader workers.

## Validation

Original author benchmark on H100, ViT-S/14, 1 GPU, 5k-sample subset with 1,314 unique SVS slides:

- Production-like worker count: about 7% iter_time improvement, 0.275s to 0.255s per step.
- 2 workers, where data loading was the bottleneck: 28% data_time reduction, 1.10s to 0.79s, with the original 4096-entry cache.

Additional review validation on `n-1` used actual shuffled SVS patch reads from `/block/TCGA/sample_dataset_30.txt`:

- `sample_dataset_30.txt`: 24,985,184 patch rows, 11,368 unique slides.
- Benchmark: 3,000 shuffled `read_region(...).convert("RGB")` reads from a 200k-row sample.

| Cache cap | Time | Samples/s | Hit rate | Process RSS |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 43.36s | 69.19 | 1.0% | ~0.99 GB |
| 512 | 43.51s | 68.94 | 3.5% | ~1.66 GB |
| 900 | 42.77s | 70.15 | 6.1% | ~2.35 GB |
| 4096 | 42.95s | 69.86 | 11.3% | ~5.31 GB |

The current 512 cap is a compromise from that validation: 4096 retained many more slide objects and used much more memory in a single process without improving this random-read throughput, while 128 had almost no reuse under shuffled sampling.

## Files changed

- `dinov2/data/datasets/slide_dataset.py`: bounded OpenSlide LRU cache, explicit close on eviction, atexit cleanup.
- `dinov2/train/train.py`: persistent workers and YAML-backed prefetch factor for the offline SVS path.

body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **3.0.4** to **7.4.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.1
   ```
   -------------------

**Bug Fixes:**

- BOM-prefixed UTF-16 and UTF-32 input now reports ``utf-16`` and
  ``utf-32`` instead of the endian-specific variants. Python's
  ``utf-16-le``/``utf-16-be``/``utf-32-le``/``utf-32-be`` codecs keep
  the BOM as a U+FEFF in the decoded string, while ``utf-16``/``utf-32``
  strip it, so callers passing the detection result directly to
  ``.decode()`` were getting a stray BOM at the start of their text.
  BOM-less UTF-16/32 detection (via null-byte patterns) is unchanged
  and still returns the endian-specific name.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `364 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/364>`_,
  `365 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/365>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Performance:**

- Switched to dense zlib-compressed model format (v2): models are now
  stored as contiguous ``memoryview`` slices of a single decompressed
  blob, eliminating per-model ``struct.unpack`` overhead. Cold start
  (import + first detect) dropped from ~75ms to ~13ms with mypyc.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `354 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/354>`_)

**Accuracy:**

- Accuracy improved from 98.6% to 99.3% (2499/2517 files) through
  a combination of training and scoring improvements:

  - Eliminated train/test data overlap by content-fingerprinting test
    suite articles and excluding them from training data
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Added MADLAD-400 and Wikipedia as supplemental training sources to
    fill gaps left by exclusion filtering
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Improved non-ASCII bigram scoring: high-byte bigrams are now
    preserved during training (instead of being crushed by global
    normalization), and weighted by per-bigram IDF so encoding-specific
    byte patterns contribute proportionally to how discriminative they
    are (`352 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/352>`_)
  - Added encoding-aware substitution filtering: character substitutions
    during training now only apply for characters the target encoding
    cannot represent
  - Increased training samples from 15K to 25K per language/encoding pair
    (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Added dedicated structural analyzers for CP932, CP949, and
  Big5-HKSCS: these superset encodings previously shared their base
  encoding's byte-range analyzer, missing extended ranges unique to each
  superset
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `353 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/353>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

**License:**

- **0BSD license** — the project license has been changed from MIT to
  `0BSD <https://opensource.org/license/0bsd>`_, a maximally permissive
  license with no attribution requirement. All prior 7.x releases
  should also be considered 0BSD licensed as of this release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Features:**

- Added ``mime_type`` field to detection results — identifies file types
  for both binary (via magic number matching) and text content. Returned
  in all ``detect()``, ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector`` results.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)
- New ``pipeline/magic.py`` module detects 40+ binary file formats
  including images, audio/video, archives, documents, executables, and
  fonts. ZIP-based formats (XLSX, DOCX, JAR, APK, EPUB, wheel,
  OpenDocument) are distinguished by entry filenames.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed incorrect equivalence between UTF-16-LE and UTF-16-BE in
  accuracy testing — these are distinct encodings with different byte
  order, not interchangeable
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Performance:**

- Added 4 new modules to mypyc compilation (orchestrator, confusion,
  magic, ascii), bringing the total to 11 compiled modules
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Capped statistical scoring at 16 KB — bigram models converge quickly,
  so large files no longer score the full 200 KB. Worst-case detection
  time dropped from 62ms to 26ms with no accuracy loss.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Replaced ``dataclasses.replace()`` with direct ``DetectionResult``
  construction on hot paths, eliminating ~354k function calls per full
  test suite run
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Build:**

- Added riscv64 to the mypyc wheel build matrix — prebuilt wheels are
  now published for RISC-V Linux alongside existing architectures
  (`Bruno Verachten <https://github.com/gounthar>`_,
  `348 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/348>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added ``include_encodings`` and ``exclude_encodings`` parameters to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — restrict or exclude specific
  encodings from the candidate set, with corresponding
  ``-i``/``--include-encodings`` and ``-x``/``--exclude-encodings``
  CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``no_match_encoding`` (default ``"cp1252"``) and
  ``empty_input_encoding`` (default ``"utf-8"``) parameters — control
  which encoding is returned when no candidate survives the pipeline or
  the input is empty, with corresponding CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``-l``/``--language`` flag to ``chardetect`` CLI — shows the
  detected language (ISO 639-1 code and English name) alongside the encoding
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `342 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/342>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `249 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `341 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_,
  `335 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/335>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now

  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `333 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/333>`_,
  `336 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/336>`_)
- Fixed undocumented encoding name changes between char

author: copilot
body:
`docker-compose.yml` used the GitHub Actions-specific `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}` variable in the `blogify-web` image reference. This variable is never set in the VPS shell environment, so it resolved to an empty string, producing the invalid image reference `ghcr.io//blogify-web:<tag>`.

## Changes

- **`docker-compose.yml`** — renamed `${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER}` to the generic `${OWNER}` in the `blogify-web` image reference, eliminating the variable-not-set warning at its source

- **`.github/workflows/cd.yml`** — updated the deploy script to pass `OWNER` inline on both `docker compose pull` and `docker compose up`, sourced from `env.OWNER` (already lowercased earlier in the workflow to match the pushed image tag)

```yaml
# Before
IMAGE_TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}" docker compose pull blogify-web
IMAGE_TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}" docker compose up -d

# After
OWNER="${{ env.OWNER }}" IMAGE_TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}" docker compose pull blogify-web
OWNER="${{ env.OWNER }}" IMAGE_TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}" docker compose up -d
```

Using `env.OWNER` (lowercased via `tr`) is intentional — GHCR requires lowercase image names and the image was pushed under the lowercased owner.

body:
💡 **What**: Refactored `useLayoutStore` calls in layout plugins and toolbar buttons to use individual state selectors instead of destructing the whole store state. Also added explanatory comments outlining the optimization.

🎯 **Why**: When destructuring from a Zustand store (e.g. `const { a, b } = useStore()`), the component will re-render whenever *any* state in the store changes, even if it's unrelated to the component. Using individual selectors (e.g. `const a = useStore(state => state.a)`) ensures the component strictly re-renders *only* when that specific state changes.

📊 **Impact**: Prevents unnecessary re-renders throughout the layout and toolbar component tree. Since the toolbar includes several atomic buttons that manage individual toggles (e.g., Ruler, Page Setup), these optimizations effectively restrict re-renders to only the exact buttons interacting with that state, improving perceived performance.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified visually through Playwright and via NextJS fast refresh/development builds. In React DevTools, toggling one layout button will no longer trigger a cascade of re-renders across all layout wrapper components and sibling layout buttons.

---
*PR created automatically by Jules for task [16541989193221881329](https://jules.google.com/task/16541989193221881329) started by @arthrod*

- Fixes https://github.com/gokcehan/lf/issues/767
- Fixes https://github.com/gokcehan/lf/issues/2490
- Follow up of https://github.com/gokcehan/lf/pull/2286

Before the move to version 3 of `Tcell`, `lf` inherited several historical terminal key ambiguities. For example, `<c-i>` was treated the same as `<tab>`, `<c-h>` as `<backspace>`, `<c-m>` as `<enter>`, and `<c-[>` as `<esc>`.

After the switch, `lf` became able to distinguish these keys as well as additional combinations such as `<c-enter>`, `<s-enter>`, and `<c-.>`. However, this was not fully taken into account when part of the key handling code was moved to `key.go`, and `<c-h>`, `<c-i>`, and `<c-m>` ended up being reported as `<c->`. This PR fixes that regression.

### Motivation
- Evitar que sidebars en modo `MxSidebarMode.Overlay` desplacen visualmente el `MainContent`, garantizando que overlays se rendericen como capas modales por encima del contenido principal. 
- Alinear la política de la ruta `/work` para exponer detalle contextual derecho como `Inline` y evitar toggles de apertura basados en selección que alteren la estructura del layout. 

### Description
- Cambiado `MxWorkspaceLayout` para que `MainRegionVisualShift`, `MainRegionVisualState` y `MainRegionVisualStateClass` sean neutrales (sin desplazamiento) y así los overlays no muevan el `MainContent` (`src/MachSoft.UI/Components/MxWorkspaceLayout.razor`).
- Actualizada la política de `ApplyRoutePolicy` y `OnShellStateChanged` en los `MainLayout` de los cuatro hosts (`Demo`/`Template` Server + Wasm) para fijar `RightSidebarMode = MxSidebarMode.Inline` en `/work` y dejar `RightSidebarOpen = false` (desacoplando la apertura de la selección) (`src/.../MainLayout.razor`).
- Ajustadas las pruebas bUnit en `MxWorkspaceLayoutTests` para validar que overlays abiertos mantienen estado visual neutral y que el backdrop/overlay se renderizan sin pérdida estructural (`tests/MachSoft.UI.Tests/MxWorkspaceLayoutTests.cs`).
- Actualizada la documentación contractual y el estado operativo (`docs/components/MxWorkspaceLayout.md`, `docs/CATALOG_EXECUTION_STATUS.md`) para reflejar la decisión: overlays no alteran la posición del `MainContainer` y `RightSidebar` en `/work` es `Inline`.

### Testing
- Ejecutado `dotnet build MachSoft.UiPlatform.sln` y la compilación completó con éxito (advertencias no nuevas relacionadas a documentación XML y resolución de paquetes). 
- Ejecutado `dotnet test tests/MachSoft.UI.Tests/MachSoft.UI.Tests.csproj --filter MxWorkspaceLayoutTests` y las pruebas relacionadas pasaron (`Passed: 21, Failed: 0`).
- No se generaron capturas de UI en este entorno (herramienta de navegador no disponible) pero la validación automatizada de comportamiento y build real se completó exitosamente.

------

body:
## Summary
  - Add configurable benchmark extension (`extensions/benchmark/circuit/`) with no-op precompiles that accept zero witnesses
  - Add standalone binary (`benchmarks/air-complexity/`) to measure proving time as a function of: number of AIRs, columns per AIR,
  constraints per AIR, and bus interactions per AIR
  - Multi-row invocations ensure precompile traces dominate system overhead; VmExe constructed directly from flat instruction sequence

author: maxghenis
body:
## Summary
- New `/usage` page with live token usage across Claude Code and Codex CLI
- Data source: https://github.com/MaxGhenis/usage-data (public repo of daily aggregates)
- Aggregates are generated locally from JSONL session files via Tokscale (no message content, file paths, or project names published)

## What the page shows
- Donut charts for 7-day / 30-day / lifetime windows, split Claude vs Codex vs other
- Daily stacked bar chart
- By-model breakdown table
- Cards linking to Tokscale and Straude public leaderboards (with the Straude embeddable SVG badge)

## Caveat built into the page
All dollar figures are computed at public API list prices. Actual out-of-pocket is a fraction of these numbers because most usage flows through ChatGPT Pro and Claude Max flat subscriptions — the page states this up front.

## Test plan
- [x] Local build succeeds (`bun run build`)
- [x] `/usage` page renders correctly in local preview
- [x] Data fetch from `raw.githubusercontent.com/MaxGhenis/usage-data/main/usage.json` works
- [ ] Verify Vercel preview deployment loads the chart, table, and donuts
